The Nigerian Air Force will hold a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony for victims of the NAF 931 aircraft crash at the National Military Cemetery, Abuja, on November 26. The ceremony will honour those who lost their lives in the October 5, 2026, crash at Igbokoda, Ondo State, and provide an opportunity for their families, colleagues and friends to pay their last respects. The Director of Public Relations and Information, NAF, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, adding that the ceremony would reaffirm the service’s respect for the departed personnel. He said, “The solemn ceremony will provide an opportunity for bereaved families, colleagues, friends and the wider NAF community to pay their last respects, honour the memories of the departed and recognise their service and sacrifice. “The wreath-laying will also serve as a formal expression of the Service’s enduring respect and remembrance for those who lost their lives in the unfortunate incident.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources Meanwhile, the Air Force said it had recovered the Cockpit Voice Recorder, alongside aircraft fragments and other relevant evidence, from the crash site. It said data retrieved from the recorder was being analysed and was expected to contribute significantly to the ongoing investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident. According to the statement, the investigation was progressing in collaboration with the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau and the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority. It attributed the difficulties encountered during the operation to the swampy nature of the terrain and the depth to which some aircraft wreckage had penetrated the ground. The statement added that the Air Force was working with relevant agencies to address environmental concerns arising from the recovery exercise and ensure appropriate remediation after its completion. The service also reiterated its commitment to supporting the bereaved families throughout the period. “The NAF recognises the profound grief experienced by the bereaved families and reiterates its commitment to providing them with sustained support throughout this difficult period,” the statement added. The Air Force assured the public that it remained committed to a thorough investigation, responsible environmental management and the dignified remembrance of those who died in the accident.
